- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility; dampen forecast by 1–4% for 7–14 days.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 3–5 consecutive days above 70); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for 5–10 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term downward trend; apply 1–3% downward adjustment if sentiment is negative or neutral over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, model tends to overforecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 2–4% for 5–10 days.
